config.title: Build memory leak detector for event listeners

intro.title: Build memory leak detector for event listeners
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple memory leak detector for event listeners in JavaScript. You will learn how to track event listeners added to DOM elements and detect potential memory leaks by checking if listeners are still attached after they should have been removed. The core programming concept involves using closures and arrays to store listener references and comparing them over time. You will work with native JavaScript constructs like addEventListener, removeEventListener, and custom tracking logic. This hands-on project will help you understand how memory leaks occur with event listeners and how to prevent them in your web applications.
intro.usecase: Event listener memory leaks are a critical issue in long-running web applications like dashboards, analytics platforms, and single-page applications. Developers encounter this problem when building interactive UI components such as real-time data filters, dynamic charts with tooltips, or multi-tab interfaces where event listeners accumulate without proper cleanup. For example, a financial dashboard that updates stock prices every second might attach new listeners with each refresh, gradually degrading performance. This lesson's memory leak detector helps identify and prevent these issues before they impact user experience in production applications.

objectives: Implement a function to track event listener registrations
Construct a mechanism to detect orphaned event listeners
Apply memory leak detection logic to DOM elements
Initialize a monitoring system for listener lifecycle
Configure cleanup procedures for detected leaks
Manipulate data structures to store listener references
Render detection results in the browser console

steps.title: Import required modules and functions
steps.instruction: Import the EventTarget and EventListener classes from the built-in 'events' module, which we'll use to create our memory leak detector.
steps.hint: Use the ES6 import syntax to import the specific classes from the 'events' module.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: importing classes from a module
import { EventEmitter } from 'events';
steps.expectedOutcome: The code will have the necessary imports to start building the memory leak detector.
successCriteria: EventTarget and EventListener are imported from the 'events' module.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported the required classes. This gives us the foundation to start building our memory leak detector.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're importing both EventTarget and EventListener from the 'events' module.
steps.feedbackWrong: That doesn't look right. You need to import EventTarget and EventListener from the built-in 'events' module using ES6 import syntax.

steps.hint: Define a function that returns an empty object for now. You can use either function declaration or arrow function syntax.

successCriteria: The function 'createMemoryLeakDetector' exists and returns an empty object.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the main detector function structure. Next we'll add tracking capabilities to it.

steps.title: Initialize tracking storage
steps.instruction: Inside your detector function, create an object named 'trackingStorage' that will store event listeners using a Map for each target.
steps.hint: You can create an empty object and assign it to a variable. This object will later hold Maps for different EventTargets.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: creating a storage object
const storage = {};
steps.expectedOutcome: The detector function now contains an empty object that will be used to track event listeners.
successCriteria: The function contains a variable declaration for 'trackingStorage' initialized as an empty object.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the storage object that will track all event listeners.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you've declared a variable named 'trackingStorage' and initialized it as an empty object inside the function.
steps.feedbackWrong: The tracking storage object is missing or incorrectly defined. Create an empty object named 'trackingStorage' inside the detector function.

steps.title: Create the addEventListener wrapper
steps.instruction: Inside the createEventListenerDetector function, create a wrapper function named addEventListenerWrapper that takes the same parameters as the native addEventListener (type, listener, options).
steps.hint: Define a function that accepts three parameters and will eventually call the original addEventListener with those parameters.
steps.expectedOutcome: The createEventListenerDetector function now contains an addEventListenerWrapper function definition.
successCriteria: The addEventListenerWrapper function is defined with three parameters (type, listener, options).
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the wrapper function that will intercept addEventListener calls.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you've defined a function named addEventListenerWrapper with three parameters.
steps.feedbackWrong: The wrapper function isn't defined correctly. Create a function named addEventListenerWrapper that accepts type, listener, and options parameters.

steps.title: Create the removeEventListener wrapper
steps.instruction: Inside the createEventListenerDetector function, create a wrapper function named removeEventListenerWrapper that intercepts removeEventListener calls.
steps.hint: Define a function that takes the same parameters as the native removeEventListener (type, listener, options) and logs or tracks the removal.
steps.expectedOutcome: A removeEventListenerWrapper function is defined inside createEventListenerDetector, ready to track removal of event listeners.
successCriteria: The removeEventListenerWrapper function is created with parameters for type, listener, and options.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the removeEventListener wrapper. This will allow us to track when listeners are removed to detect potential leaks.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've started the wrapper, but make sure it's a function that can intercept removeEventListener calls with appropriate parameters.
steps.feedbackWrong: The removeEventListener wrapper wasn't created correctly. Check that you've defined a function inside createEventListenerDetector that can handle removeEventListener parameters.

steps.title: Create the leak detection function
steps.instruction: Inside the createEventListenerDetector function, create a new function named detectLeaks that returns an array of potential leak objects.
steps.hint: Define detectLeaks as a function that will analyze the tracked listeners and return results.
steps.expectedOutcome: The detectLeaks function is defined inside createEventListenerDetector, ready to implement leak analysis logic.
successCriteria: A function named detectLeaks is created inside createEventListenerDetector and returns an array.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the detectLeaks function. Next we'll implement the leak analysis logic inside it.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure detectLeaks is defined as a function that returns an array.
steps.feedbackWrong: The detectLeaks function should be defined inside createEventListenerDetector and return an array.

steps.title: Create the cleanup function
steps.instruction: Inside the createEventListenerDetector function, create a function named cleanup that removes all tracked listeners and restores the original addEventListener and removeEventListener methods.
steps.hint: The cleanup function should iterate through the tracked listeners, call removeEventListener on each, clear the tracking storage, and restore the native methods.
steps.expectedOutcome: The cleanup function is defined inside createEventListenerDetector and will be used to clean up tracked listeners and restore native methods.
successCriteria: A function named cleanup is created inside createEventListenerDetector with the logic to remove tracked listeners and restore original methods.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the cleanup function. This function will handle removing all tracked listeners and restoring the native methods when needed.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've started creating the cleanup function, but make sure it's named 'cleanup' and includes logic to remove tracked listeners and restore original methods.
steps.feedbackWrong: The cleanup function is missing or incorrectly implemented. It should be named 'cleanup' and contain the logic to clean up tracked listeners and restore native methods.

steps.title: Create the reporting function
steps.instruction: Inside the createEventListenerDetector function, create a function named reportLeaks that returns a formatted string describing the detected leaks.
steps.hint: The reportLeaks function should call the leak detection function you created earlier and format its results into a readable string.
steps.expectedOutcome: The createEventListenerDetector function will contain a reportLeaks function that formats leak detection results as a string.
successCriteria: A reportLeaks function is defined inside createEventListenerDetector and returns a string based on leak detection results.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the reporting function that will format leak information for display.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a function, but make sure it's named reportLeaks and returns a formatted string using the leak detection results.
steps.feedbackWrong: The reportLeaks function is missing or doesn't return a formatted string. Try creating a function that calls your leak detection function and formats the results.

steps.title: Set up the detector initialization
steps.instruction: Inside the createEventListenerDetector function, create an initialization function named initializeDetector that sets up the wrappers and returns them.
steps.hint: The initializeDetector function should return an object containing the wrapped addEventListener and removeEventListener functions.
steps.expectedOutcome: The initializeDetector function is defined inside createEventListenerDetector and returns an object with the wrapped event listener functions.
successCriteria: The initializeDetector function is created and returns an object containing the wrapped addEventListener and removeEventListener functions.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! The initializeDetector function is properly set up to return the wrapped event listener functions.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've created the initializeDetector function, but make sure it returns an object with the wrapped addEventListener and removeEventListener functions.
steps.feedbackWrong: The initializeDetector function is missing or doesn't return the required wrapped functions. Review the instruction and try again.

steps.title: Export the detector functions
steps.instruction: Export the createEventListenerDetector function so it can be imported and used in other modules.
steps.hint: Use the export keyword before the function declaration, or add an export statement after it.
steps.expectedOutcome: The createEventListenerDetector function is exported, making the memory leak detector available for import in other JavaScript files.
successCriteria: The createEventListenerDetector function is exported using either export function createEventListenerDetector() {} or export { createEventListenerDetector }.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully exported the detector function. Now other modules can import and use your memory leak detector.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're exporting the function named createEventListenerDetector so it can be imported elsewhere.
steps.feedbackWrong: The function isn't properly exported. Check that you're using the export keyword with the correct function name.
